newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 24.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 24.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:

** Jardine Fleming has put India in the 'overweight' category after a gap of more than eight months. India's rating has now been upgraded from the 'neutral' category, which may imply allocation of more funds to India among the emerging markets, the Economic Times reports.

** Essar Steel will go in for an upfront credit arrangement of $100 million with the $1.8 billion U.S.-based Commercial Metal Corporation's trading arm based in Switzerland, for the export of its hot-rolled coils, the Financial Express reports.

** Siemens Ltd, the 11.86 billion rupee Indian affiliate of the German multinational Siemens AG has embarked on a major restructuring programme to stem the losses arising out of a substantial slowdown in the demand for some of its major products, the Economic Times says.
The paper says the programme includes large scale
curtailment of fresh investments, retrenchment of excess workforce, shedding of unproductive assets and minimising even the essential expenses.

** India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index rose to 7.99 percent in the week ending February 8 from 7.73 percent in the previous week, the Industry Ministry said on Sunday.
** The Indian rupee opened steady on Monday at 35.89/90 and is seen range-bound, dealers said. The day's range is seen at 35/88/91 rupees to a dollar, they said.
** Subdued sentiment ahead of Friday's budget is expected to depress Indian shares this week, but lingering optimism could prevent heavy losses, analysts said at the weekend.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will present the 1997/98
(April-March) budget to Parliament on February 28, against a backdrop of inflation edging up as industrial growth slows.
Last week the BSE's benchmark 30-share index
tumbled 82 points, or nearly 2.3 percent, in lacklustre trade, to close at 3,439.49 on Friday.
